t: You're looking at the Queen's Chapel, a Grade I listed building and part of the royal household's religious establishment, the Chapel Royal. It was designed by Inigo Jones and built between 1623 and 1625, next to St James's Palace. It was originally meant as a Catholic chapel for the Infanta Maria Anna of Spain, but she never used it, because she did not marry King Charles I. It was used instead by Queen Henrietta Maria of France, who was Catholic, and her retinue. Later it served various continental Protestants living at Court. Don't confuse it with the older Chapel Royal, just across Marlborough Road.
